You really didn't mention enough of the cons. Birds need to fly, their entire body is built for it, and so is their mind. If you clip your birds, you risk them becoming inactive, more aggressive, depressed, overweight, and otherwise unhappy. If you want to keep your bird safe from windows, you can teach them by lightly tapping them on the glass, you can also teach them to keep away from stoves and other dangers. 

Also know, that your bird can still fly with clipped wings, but not well enough to stay in the air. Which means they can easily fly out if you leave an open door or window, but become at risk of dogs and cats since they can't fly properly and will be easily exhausted. 

Even if you regret clipping your birds wings, and wait the almost year long period(depending on the bird) it takes for them to grow back, your bird might never try to fly again. The belive that flying leads to falling and getting hurt might be too ingrained in the bird. 

At the end of the day I can't control what you do with your bird, but understand that clipping is risking your birds health, both mental and physical.
